topic: The Additive Property of Normal Distributions: Gaussian + Gaussian = Gaussian

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Shape of Certainty
lecture_lines: A normal distribution is defined by mean and variance.
The mean represents the center of the distribution.
The variance defines the spread or noise level.
Visually, we represent this as a bell curve.
It shows certainty centered around the mean.
animations: Create a single Gaussian curve centered at mu=0, sigma=1 with color #FFFFFF.
Highlight the area under the curve in light blue #ADD8E6 to represent 1-unit certainty.
Transition the curve to bold #FFD700 to emphasize the standard base state.

sections.title: The Problem: Adding Two Independent Random Variables
lecture_lines: What happens when we add two independent variables?
Imagine two distinct bell curves representing noise.
They move toward each other to merge.
This represents combined uncertainty in total time.
Can we describe this sum as a new distribution?
animations: Display two separate Gaussian curves side-by-side in white #FFFFFF.
Label them 'Variable X' and 'Variable Y' in white #FFFFFF.
Show the two curves moving toward each other to merge.

sections.title: The Rule: Summation of Parameters
lecture_lines: The sum of two independent gaussians is gaussian.
The new mean is the sum of means.
The new variance is the sum of variances.
Note that variances add, not standard deviations.
This creates a predictable model for total time.
animations: Show two Gaussian variables with parameters (mu1, sigma1^2) and (mu2, sigma2^2) in white #FFFFFF.
Display the sum formula: mu_sum = mu1 + mu2, sigma_sum^2 = sigma1^2 + sigma2^2.
Animate the transformation of the two curves into a final sum curve in gold #FFD700.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Broadening'
lecture_lines: Adding noise increases total system uncertainty.
Two narrow curves combine into a wider bell.
The peak becomes flatter as variance grows.
animations: Display a narrow Gaussian curve #FFFFFF, representing low variance.
Show a wider Gaussian curve #FFFFFF, representing higher variance.
Animate the 'broadening' effect as the variance increases, color changing to #FF6347.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Summing independent gaussians is a closed operation.
This property is crucial for sensor fusion.
It predicts combined error in real-world systems.
animations: Summarize the summation rule with a simple table showing input parameters vs. sum.
Highlight the resulting sum curve in bright green #90EE90 to show final combined result.
Fade out the elements while showing a real-world icon (e.g., error margin).
